claims.text: This trip was sold on an upfront quote: EV-FARE-00516 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 43.10 and charged_total 46.10. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so the only sum the rider can recover on this trip is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That excess is exactly SGD 3.00, it is the single ERP line, and POL-RD-11(a) refunds it in full.

The ERP charge is a phantom line. EV-FARE-00516 bills SGD 3.00 for the gantry 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' at 1.296, 103.822, but the platform's own comparison of that gantry against the trace puts the nearest fix 2608.77 m away at 13:25:40, with gap_brackets_closest_approach false (EV-GPS-00516, derived.erp_gantry_proximity). POL-RD-09 treats a fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing; the gantry carries coordinates, so the match is decidable rather than undecidable, and on this trace the vehicle never comes near it. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure and the line is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists.

The mismatch cannot be explained away as missing data. EV-GPS-00516 covers 100% of the trip: 169 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 13:06:40 to 13:34:40, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so the trace does not meet any of the impairment limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07. The absence of any fix near the gantry is therefore a fact about where the vehicle actually drove, not a hole in the record, and the billing-integrity finding rests on clean evidence.

The optimal route for this trip carries no ERP at all: EV-TRIP-00516 records optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, and EV-FARE-00516's own derived block reports on_optimal_route_total 0.00 against off_optimal_route_total 3.00, with the gantry flagged on_optimal_route false. The SGD 3.00 charged to the rider is thus entirely a charge for a corridor the platform's own optimal route does not use, and it is not a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09 or a charge the quoted fare comprehended under POL-RD-11.

The rider concedes the distance point. On this trip's own trace the excess is 0.6 km and 5.36% (EV-GPS-00516, derived.deviation, against the booked optimal of 11.2 km), which fails both limbs of POL-RD-01 — greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km absolute — so no route deviation is established and no distance or time refund is sought. POL-RD-01 nevertheless preserves the billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) whether or not a deviation exists, so the SGD 3.00 survives that finding.

The driver's explanation that traffic on the expressway got bad points to no artifact. EV-ADVIS-00516-01, the only traffic advisory in the bundle, is MISSING: it has no payload and weight_multiplier 0.0, so there is no advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses as POL-RD-03(a) requires. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08. This claim rests on an artifact at weight 0.0 and is disclosed as such.

POL-RD-04 does not run against the rider either. The four route-change messages in EV-CHAT-00516 (MSG-00516-001 to MSG-00516-004) were all sent by the DRIVER, every message on the trip carries waypoint_hint null, and the rider's only message is 'ok fine' (MSG-00516-005) — no place and no road named. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction specifically enough to act on, and where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable; nothing in the chat is a rider request for the route the driver took.

Because no deviation is established, there is no excess for POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 to excuse, so no exculpatory clause has any work to do on this trip and the only live question is the off-route ERP line. POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from escalation a charge line with no counterpart in the trace where that line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4). This is therefore a case the tribunal can decide with money rather than one it must hold, and the outcome on the SGD 3.00 is determinable on the record.

EV-RPROF-00516 records rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d as 0, well below the 4-or-more trigger in POL-RD-08, so the heightened-corroboration condition in that clause is not engaged and this rider's claim is not subject to any requirement of corroboration beyond the trace.

No route deviation is established under POL-RD-01, so the rider's core claim fails at the threshold. The trace governs, and it records 11.8 km between the pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 11.2 km - an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute; 0.6 km fails both limbs, and the derived deviation finding on the trace is literally 'no deviation'. Whatever the rider says about red lights and expressways, no refundable deviation exists.

Even measured against the amended route the rider herself accepted, there is no deviation. The trip record carries dropoff_amended_at of 2026-09-04T13:10:40+08:00 - five seconds after the rider typed 'ok fine' - and an amended_optimal_distance_km of 11.6 km. Re-applying POL-RD-01 against those amended endpoints leaves an excess of just 0.2 km, further below the 0.8 km and 20% gates. The route the rider actually authorised is the closest fit to the route driven.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace is unimpaired on its face - 100% coverage, 169 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds - and it shows only 0.6 km of excess. The burden is not discharged, and because no deviation is established the driver has no exculpatory clause to invoke and none is needed.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 43.10, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. No distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess would have been. The 43.10 of base, distance, time and platform charges stands untouched.

The only amount by which the charge exceeds the agreed quote is 3.00: charged_total of 46.10 less quoted_fare of 43.10, which is exactly the single ERP line. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only monetary claim on an upfront trip is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, so the 43.10 quoted fare is not in issue at all and the rider's contested figure of 46.10 is not recoverable as a whole.

On the single ERP line the driver puts the honest case rather than a stretch. The line is 3.00 for the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) gantry; the fare record itself marks it as not on the optimal route, and its nearest trace fix is 2608 m away, far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses. On this record that line is unmatched, and POL-RD-09(4) makes it a standalone billing-integrity correction of 3.00 which is available whether or not a deviation exists. That 3.00 is the whole and entire extent of any refund; it does not disturb the quoted fare, and no POL-RD-02 refund is layered on top of it.

This case is determinate and needs no escalation. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00516), the trace is unimpaired and gap-free, there is no timestamp conflict beyond 10 minutes, and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the ERP line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly excluded from the POL-RD-10(8) escalation trigger. No POL-RD-10 limb fires, so the dispute should be ruled on the merits rather than sent to a human reviewer.

The rider's coercion framing is not what the chat log shows. The driver asked whether she would accept a new route and the rider replied 'ok fine' at 13:10:35, after which the app recorded the amended route and the amended optimal. A route change accepted in-app is the authorised baseline, which is why POL-RD-05's amended optimal governs; nothing in the route-deviation policy makes an accepted route change a ground of refund, and POL-RD-11 places any unrecovered cost of an unjustified detour on the driver rather than the rider. The driver is not reaching for extra money here.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you are getting back the one charge you should not have paid, and nothing more. To the driver: your route on this trip was within tolerance, and the only deduction is a toll line the vehicle never incurred.

DISTANCE. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00516) covers the whole trip — 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 seconds — and records 11.8 km driven against a booked optimal of 11.2 km: an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute. Neither limb is met, so no route deviation is established and no distance or time refund is available. Measured against the amended route you accepted (amended_optimal_distance_km 11.6 km, dropoff amended at 13:10:40), the excess is only 0.2 km, so the answer does not change.

FARE. This was an upfront-quoted trip: quoted_fare_sgd SGD 43.10, charged_total SGD 46.10. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run, so those lines are not in issue.

TOLL. The only charged line outside the quote is SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' gantry. The fare breakdown itself marks that gantry as not on the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total 3.00 against on_optimal_route_total 0.00), the trip record's optimal route carries no ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and the gantry carries coordinates (1.296, 103.822) against which the platform compared the trace: the nearest fix is 2,608.77 m away, far outside POL-RD-09's 250 m crossing radius. The vehicle never passed the gantry. Because the gantry has coordinates the match is decidable, so POL-RD-09(4) applies: the SGD 3.00 is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. POL-RD-11(a) reaches the same figure. That SGD 3.00 is the entire refund and is not layered on any distance refund (POL-RD-09(1)); it exceeds the SGD 0.50 de minimis.

POINTS THAT DID NOT MOVE THE MONEY. The rider's account that she was pressed into accepting the route change, and the driver's that expressway traffic turned bad and he took local roads, do not alter the arithmetic. Because the trace shows no material excess, the question whether the route change was freely accepted or urged on her decides nothing about the money, and the driver's traffic explanation cites no traffic advisory — the only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 — so it cannot excuse a deviation (POL-RD-03) and has no bearing on the toll line. No escalation is required: the trip identifiers all match (TRP-00516 on trip record, trace and fare breakdown), the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the ERP line, which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes because it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4).

Because a billing-integrity defect is present, the case is also referred under POL-RD-09(4), which does not disturb the money above.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver:

This was an upfront-quoted trip (EV-FARE-00516: fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 43.10, charged_total 46.10). Under POL-RD-11 the base, distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02's recomputation does not run and the SGD 43.10 quote is not refundable on distance or time however the route is described; the rider's request for the whole SGD 46.10 cannot succeed on that ground. The driver's POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-09 claims on this point are accepted.

On distance both sides in fact agree and the record confirms it. The trace governs (POL-RD-01): gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.8 km against a booked optimal of 11.2 km — an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% — and against the amended optimal of 11.6 km adopted when the dropoff was amended at 13:10:40 an excess of only 0.2 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km; neither limb is met, so no deviation is established and no distance-or-time refund arises. With no excess established there is nothing for POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 to excuse. POL-RD-04 is in any event unavailable: the four route-change messages were all sent by the driver, every waypoint_hint is null, no road or place was named, and the rider's only message was 'ok fine' — so the accepted route change is the authorised baseline and no rider-requested detour can be read into the chat.

What remains, and what decides the case, is the single ERP line. The fare breakdown charged SGD 3.00 for the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) gantry, but the platform's own comparison of that gantry against a trace covering 100% of the trip (169 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps) puts the nearest fix 2,608.77 m away — far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses. The gantry carries coordinates, so the match is decidable rather than undecidable, and on this trace the vehicle never crossed it; the optimal route for the trip also carries no ERP at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, on_optimal_route false, off_optimal_route_total 3.00). Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure and the SGD 3.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. It is also exactly the excess of charged_total (46.10) over quoted_fare (43.10), so under POL-RD-11(a) the same SGD 3.00 is the entire amount recoverable; both sides are right that the figure is 3.00, and it is counted once, not layered.

The driver's account that expressway traffic turned bad and justified local roads is noted but points to no artifact. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and a general assertion of bad traffic does not discharge the driver's position (POL-RD-08). It neither exonerates the ERP nor changes the money. No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (11.8 km) is not less than the distance traced, so POL-RD-04's second limb has nothing to compute.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); no timestamps conflict; and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 0) does not engage the heightened-corroboration condition, and it is citable only for that test.

The driver's conduct in pressing the route change is not a money ground here and no POL-RD-06(c) referral arises, because no MATERIAL deviation was established and no pattern appears. The billing-integrity finding is referred under POL-RD-09(4), which does not delay or displace this ruling.

Outcome: SGD 3.00 of the contested SGD 46.10 is refunded to the rider; the remaining SGD 43.10 quoted fare stands; nothing is owed to the driver.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 3.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) ERP line on TRP-00516 was charged although no GPS fix comes within the 250 m match radius (nearest fix 2,608.77 m, on a 100%-coverage trace). The line is refunded in full as a standalone correction and the ERP billing for this trip should be reviewed.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is a route-deviation dispute over TRP-00516, on which SGD 46.10 was charged. I find no refundable distance deviation, but SGD 3.00 of the ERP charge is refunded to the rider.

No route deviation (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace EV-GPS-00516 (weight 1.0) is clean and governs: 11.8 km between the pickup and dropoff events against the booked optimal of 11.2 km, an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km absolute and 20% of optimal; 0.6 km and 5.36% fail both gates. Measured against the amended optimal of 11.6 km the excess is only 0.2 km. So no distance or time refund arises on the deviation route, and the rider's own advocate concedes this. Because the fare was an UPFRONT_QUOTE (EV-FARE-00516: quoted_fare_sgd 43.10), POL-RD-11 applies and POL-RD-02 does not run at all: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines.

The ERP line is refunded (POL-RD-09(4)). The fare charged SGD 3.00 for the gantry 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)'. The platform's own comparison places the nearest trace fix 2608.77 m away, the gantry is flagged off the optimal route, and the optimal route carries SGD 0.00 of ERP. The line is therefore a charge for a gantry the trace never passes: a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. This is also the whole amount by which the charge exceeds the agreed quote: charged_total 46.10 less quoted_fare 43.10 = 3.00, and it is the same SGD 3.00 counted once, not twice (POL-RD-09(1)).

The driver's explanation that expressway traffic turned bad is unsupported. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00516-01, is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 and names nothing, so under POL-RD-08 the bare assertion carries no weight; and it needs none, because there is no excess for POL-RD-03 to excuse. The rider's account of being pressed to accept the route change is borne out by the chat (EV-CHAT-00516, where the rider's only message is 'ok fine'), but acceptance of a route change is not itself a ground of refund, no message names a place or road and waypoint_hint is null throughout, so POL-RD-04 cannot run, and POL-RD-11 places any unrecovered detour cost on the driver rather than the rider. Neither party's profile changes anything; rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no heightened-corroboration condition is engaged.

Confidence: the deciding facts — that the trip is upfront-quoted and that the ERP gantry was never crossed — are carried by EV-GPS-00516 and EV-FARE-00516, both at weight_multiplier 1.0 and independent of each other (device trace versus payments ledger), so the cap is 1.0. The refund is SGD 3.00 of the contested SGD 46.10 — a partial refund; the remaining SGD 43.10 stands. The billing-integrity finding is referred for review as POL-RD-09(4) requires.

ruling.explanation:
Rider against driver, trip TRP-00516: your dispute is partly upheld. Of the SGD 46.10 you contested, SGD 3.00 is refunded.

THE MONEY FIGURES. EV-FARE-00516 records an upfront quote (quoted_fare_sgd) of SGD 43.10 and a charged_total of SGD 46.10. The entire SGD 3.00 difference is one line: the ERP charge for gantry 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)', SGD 3.00, charged at 13:22:40.

THE TOLL LINE IS REFUNDED. That gantry carries coordinates (1.296, 103.822). Compared against the GPS trace, the nearest fix is 2,608.77 m away at 13:25:40, and the platform records gap_brackets_closest_approach as false. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; the gantry has coordinates, so the match is decidable and the vehicle never came within 2.6 km of it. This is not a hole in the record: EV-GPS-00516 covers 100% of the trip with 169 fixes at a 10-second cadence, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it meets none of the impairment limbs POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The line is therefore a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. It is also exactly the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare, which POL-RD-11(a) refunds once the pass-through is not properly chargeable (optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00 and the gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false). Both routes reach the same SGD 3.00, and it is counted once, not twice.

NO DISTANCE OR TIME REFUND. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so under POL-RD-11 the base, distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run; no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. In any event no deviation is established. The governing figure under POL-RD-01 is the trace (11.8 km), not the rounded trip-record copy, and against the booked optimal of 11.2 km the excess is 0.6 km, or 5.4% — below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km absolute and 20%. Against the amended dropoff it is smaller still (0.2 km against the amended optimal of 11.6 km). With no deviation there is nothing for POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 to excuse, and the rider accepts the distance point.

THE ROUTE-CHANGE ACCOUNT. The chat log bears out that the driver pressed for the change — four driver messages (MSG-00516-001 to 004), ending with your 'ok fine' at 13:10:35 (MSG-00516-005), after which the app recorded the amended dropoff at 13:10:40. The rider's account of being pressed is credited, but nothing in the route-deviation policy makes an accepted route change a ground of refund on the distance lines: POL-RD-05 makes the amended route the authorised baseline, and POL-RD-04 does not apply because every message is the driver's, every message carries waypoint_hint null, and no rider instruction names a place or road. What the rider is owed for the expressway she was told she would take and did not is the toll line, and that is the SGD 3.00 refunded.

BURDEN AND PROFILES. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold from an unimpaired trace; that is not shown and the rider concedes it. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 0) is below the 4-or-more trigger, so no heightened corroboration applies. The driver's profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 of completed_trips_90d 250) shows no repeat-deviation pattern, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no material deviation, no conduct referral and no uplift. No driver compensation is payable either — the fare billed 11.8 km, matching the trace, so there is no unbilled shortfall.

NO ESCALATION. Under POL-RD-10 the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown (all TRP-00516), the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the ERP line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly excluded by POL-RD-10(8). The driver's statement that expressway traffic worsened is unsupported by any artifact — there is no traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00516-01 is MISSING) — but no deviation was ever established, so no exculpatory clause had to run and no POL-RD-10(5) trigger fires. The case is decided on the merits with money.

ledger.claim: This trip was sold on an upfront quote: EV-FARE-00516 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 43.10 and charged_total 46.10. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so the only sum the rider can recover on this trip is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That excess is exactly SGD 3.00, it is the single ERP line, and POL-RD-11(a) refunds it in full.

The ERP charge is a phantom line. EV-FARE-00516 bills SGD 3.00 for the gantry 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City)' at 1.296, 103.822, but the platform's own comparison of that gantry against the trace puts the nearest fix 2608.77 m away at 13:25:40, with gap_brackets_closest_approach false (EV-GPS-00516, derived.erp_gantry_proximity). POL-RD-09 treats a fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing; the gantry carries coordinates, so the match is decidable rather than undecidable, and on this trace the vehicle never comes near it. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure and the line is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists.

The mismatch cannot be explained away as missing data. EV-GPS-00516 covers 100% of the trip: 169 fixes at a 10 s cadence from 13:06:40 to 13:34:40, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so the trace does not meet any of the impairment limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07. The absence of any fix near the gantry is therefore a fact about where the vehicle actually drove, not a hole in the record, and the billing-integrity finding rests on clean evidence.

The optimal route for this trip carries no ERP at all: EV-TRIP-00516 records optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, and EV-FARE-00516's own derived block reports on_optimal_route_total 0.00 against off_optimal_route_total 3.00, with the gantry flagged on_optimal_route false. The SGD 3.00 charged to the rider is thus entirely a charge for a corridor the platform's own optimal route does not use, and it is not a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09 or a charge the quoted fare comprehended under POL-RD-11.

The rider concedes the distance point. On this trip's own trace the excess is 0.6 km and 5.36% (EV-GPS-00516, derived.deviation, against the booked optimal of 11.2 km), which fails both limbs of POL-RD-01 — greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km absolute — so no route deviation is established and no distance or time refund is sought. POL-RD-01 nevertheless preserves the billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) whether or not a deviation exists, so the SGD 3.00 survives that finding.

The driver's explanation that traffic on the expressway got bad points to no artifact. EV-ADVIS-00516-01, the only traffic advisory in the bundle, is MISSING: it has no payload and weight_multiplier 0.0, so there is no advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses as POL-RD-03(a) requires. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08. This claim rests on an artifact at weight 0.0 and is disclosed as such.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-04 does not run against the rider either. The four route-change messages in EV-CHAT-00516 (MSG-00516-001 to MSG-00516-004) were all sent by the DRIVER, every message on the trip carries waypoint_hint null, and the rider's only message is 'ok fine' (MSG-00516-005) — no place and no road named. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction specifically enough to act on, and where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable; nothing in the chat is a rider request for the route the driver took.

Because no deviation is established, there is no excess for POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 to excuse, so no exculpatory clause has any work to do on this trip and the only live question is the off-route ERP line. POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from escalation a charge line with no counterpart in the trace where that line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4). This is therefore a case the tribunal can decide with money rather than one it must hold, and the outcome on the SGD 3.00 is determinable on the record.

EV-RPROF-00516 records rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d as 0, well below the 4-or-more trigger in POL-RD-08, so the heightened-corroboration condition in that clause is not engaged and this rider's claim is not subject to any requirement of corroboration beyond the trace.

No route deviation is established under POL-RD-01, so the rider's core claim fails at the threshold. The trace governs, and it records 11.8 km between the pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 11.2 km - an excess of 0.6 km, or 5.36% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute; 0.6 km fails both limbs, and the derived deviation finding on the trace is literally 'no deviation'. Whatever the rider says about red lights and expressways, no refundable deviation exists.

Even measured against the amended route the rider herself accepted, there is no deviation. The trip record carries dropoff_amended_at of 2026-09-04T13:10:40+08:00 - five seconds after the rider typed 'ok fine' - and an amended_optimal_distance_km of 11.6 km. Re-applying POL-RD-01 against those amended endpoints leaves an excess of just 0.2 km, further below the 0.8 km and 20% gates. The route the rider actually authorised is the closest fit to the route driven.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace is unimpaired on its face - 100% coverage, 169 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds - and it shows only 0.6 km of excess. The burden is not discharged, and because no deviation is established the driver has no exculpatory clause to invoke and none is needed.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 43.10, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. No distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess would have been. The 43.10 of base, distance, time and platform charges stands untouched.

The only amount by which the charge exceeds the agreed quote is 3.00: charged_total of 46.10 less quoted_fare of 43.10, which is exactly the single ERP line. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only monetary claim on an upfront trip is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, so the 43.10 quoted fare is not in issue at all and the rider's contested figure of 46.10 is not recoverable as a whole.

On the single ERP line the driver puts the honest case rather than a stretch. The line is 3.00 for the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards City) gantry; the fare record itself marks it as not on the optimal route, and its nearest trace fix is 2608 m away, far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses. On this record that line is unmatched, and POL-RD-09(4) makes it a standalone billing-integrity correction of 3.00 which is available whether or not a deviation exists. That 3.00 is the whole and entire extent of any refund; it does not disturb the quoted fare, and no POL-RD-02 refund is layered on top of it.

This case is determinate and needs no escalation. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00516), the trace is unimpaired and gap-free, there is no timestamp conflict beyond 10 minutes, and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the ERP line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly excluded from the POL-RD-10(8) escalation trigger. No POL-RD-10 limb fires, so the dispute should be ruled on the merits rather than sent to a human reviewer.

The rider's coercion framing is not what the chat log shows. The driver asked whether she would accept a new route and the rider replied 'ok fine' at 13:10:35, after which the app recorded the amended route and the amended optimal. A route change accepted in-app is the authorised baseline, which is why POL-RD-05's amended optimal governs; nothing in the route-deviation policy makes an accepted route change a ground of refund, and POL-RD-11 places any unrecovered cost of an unjustified detour on the driver rather than the rider. The driver is not reaching for extra money here.
